theory.title: Conditionals and concession
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 051. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Conditionals and concession
patterns.pattern: if / unless / provided that / although
examples: If access improves, participation will rise.
Although the plan is costly, it may be worthwhile.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

phrases.english: A key issue is how decisions are justified.

phrases.english: There is more to consider than first appears.

content.passage: The question of 051 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 051 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. theory.title: Participle clauses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 053. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Participle clauses
patterns.pattern: -ing / having + past participle
examples: Having considered both sides, she changed her mind.
Faced with criticism, he responded calmly.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 053 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

content.passage: The question of 054 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. theory.title: Hedging and advanced linking
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 055. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Hedging and advanced linking
patterns.pattern: tend to / arguably / nevertheless / to some extent
examples: The proposal seems to address the main concern.
Arguably, context matters more than first impressions.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 055 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

content.passage: The question of 056 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 056 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Past perfect and narrative tenses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 057. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Past perfect and narrative tenses
patterns.pattern: had + past participle / had been + -ing
examples: They had already discussed the issue.
She had been reflecting on the decision for weeks.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 057 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 057 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Wish and if only
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 058. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Wish and if only
patterns.pattern: wish / if only + past or past perfect

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 058 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 058 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Advanced relative clauses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 059. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Advanced relative clauses
patterns.pattern: which / whose / whereby / in which
examples: The colleague, whose judgement I value, challenged the idea.
It was a decision in which everyone had a say.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 059 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 059 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Passive forms and reporting
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 060. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Passive forms and reporting
patterns.pattern: be + past participle / it is reported that
examples: The proposal was approved after consultation.
It is widely believed that early support matters.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

phrases.english: A key issue is how decisions are justified.
phrases.spanish: Una cuestión clave es cómo se justifican las decisiones.

phrases.english: There is more to consider than first appears.

content.passage: The question of 060 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 060 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.
